quote.translation: Everything other than the unmoved mover is moved by another, and so "has the contingency of being otherwise" (ἐνδέχεται ἄλλως ἔχειν); it is, in other words, metaphysical contingency as the negation of metaphysical necessity.

quote.translation: These concepts of metaphysical necessity and metaphysical contingency are nothing other than the application of disjunctive necessity and disjunctive contingency to the metaphysical horizon, and in the Middle Ages they were taken up by Moses Maimonides, a venerator of Aristotle, and put to use as a moment in the "cosmological proof" of the existence of God.

Thomas Aquinas, following Maimonides, likewise inferred from the contingency of the world to "something that is necessary through itself" (aliquid quod est per se necessarium) (Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I. 2.
